facts.business: Integrated Thermoplastics Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of thermoplastic products.

auditor.name: Grandhy & Co., Chartered Accountants
auditor.emphasis_or_qualification: 1. Amounts receivables and payables subject to confirmation and reconciliation. 2. Internal Auditor not appointed as per Section 138. 3. Significant fixed costs incurred despite decline in turnover. 4. OTS arrangements with Union Bank of India and APSFC; Rs 29.12 crore received from group companies without formal agreement. 5. Disproportionately high outstanding creditors (Rs 26.85 crore) vs material consumption (Rs 2.22 crore); Rs 22.59 crore outstanding >1 year. 6. Accumulated losses of Rs 59.99 crore, net worth fully eroded. 7. Default on APSFC loan; interest not provided. 8. NCLT case by SP Coal Resources Pvt Ltd pending. 9. Union Bank loans classified NPA; interest not provided. 10. Land title dispute case pending in City Civil Court, Medak.

key_risks: Accumulated losses of Rs 59.99 crore and fully eroded net worth raising going concern uncertainty
Non-appointment of Managing Director/CEO/Whole-time Director as required for listed company
DINs of three independent directors deactivated on MCA records
Independent directors not registered in Independent Directors Databank
No separate meeting of independent directors held during the year
Internal Complaints Committee not constituted under POSH Act
Receivables and payables subject to confirmation and reconciliation
High outstanding creditors (Rs 26.85 crore) with Rs 22.59 crore overdue >1 year
OTS with banks and receipt of Rs 29.12 crore from group companies without formal agreements
Default on APSFC and Union Bank loans; interest not provided in books
Pending NCLT case by operational creditor SP Coal Resources Pvt Ltd
Land title dispute case pending in City Civil Court, Medak
facts.related_party_note: The Company entered into One-Time Settlement (OTS) arrangements with Union Bank of India and Andhra Pradesh State Finance Corporation (APSFC) and paid Rs 20.17 crore towards settlement. An amount of Rs 29.12 crore was received from group companies, but no formal inter-company agreement has been entered into for such transactions.
